# Rules and codes

Scripts are checked for structure, meaning and in a dry run (a simulation). Errors (E_) reject the script; warnings (W_) are allowed. Every error comes back with its path and a fix.

## Key rules
- Only the fields in 01_script_format.md; never invent fields ("description", "notes", "type", a beat "duration"). Numbers are not quoted; colors are "#rrggbb"; facing is 1 or -1.
- Ids: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter (v1 up to 24 characters, v2 32), unique; story beat ids are unique across the story.
- A character beat's "do" is a move; a world beat ("who": "world") does a world command and never has target, outcome, approach or say.
- Attacks take target, outcome and "approach": "run"; paired moves need a partner; "needs" means that prop is held.
- Params are only the listed ones (loops also take distance and cycles); world params include every required (*) one.
- A knocked-out or defeated character cannot act until get_up or return.
- Text is plain Latin letters, digits and punctuation: say 40 characters, text_pop 16, caption 80, narration 160, dialogue lines 120.
- Character colors must stand out on the theme background (05_places_and_objects.md).

## Before you answer, check
1. One JSON object, nothing else; the version, ids and locations are the ones the task gives.
2. Everyone who acts is in characters (clip) or in the scene's cast (story), placed on the stage.
3. Every id is lowercase_with_underscores and unique; every reference points at a beat in the same scene.
4. Every attack with a target has "approach": "run" and an outcome; paired moves have a partner.
5. No target, outcome, approach or say on world beats or non-attack moves.
6. Move, macro and world params use the listed names; required ones are present.
7. Faces, moves, objects, activities, moods, fx and themes come from the pack files.
8. Nobody acts after a KO or defeat without get_up or return.
9. Colors stand out on the background; the first camera key is at 0.
10. The clip or story ends clearly: a victory, a KO, an end card or a fade.


## Limits

Clips: up to 6 characters, 600 beats, 3-900 s. Stories: up to 16 in the cast, 8 on stage, 40 scenes, 20 locations, 12 extras, 200 beats a scene, scenes up to 300 s, at most 900 s in all.

## Validator codes

- E_VERSION: version is not 1, 2 or 3 → 1 for a clip, 2 for a story, 3 for a story with depth.
- E_SCHEMA_TYPE: wrong JSON type → Numbers unquoted, lists in [], objects in {}.
- E_SCHEMA_REQUIRED: a required field is missing → Add the field the message names.
- E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN_FIELD: a field that does not exist → Remove it or use the suggested name.
- E_SCHEMA_ENUM: a value not in the allowed list → Use a value the message lists.
- E_SCHEMA_RANGE: a number out of range or a character placed off the stage → Stay in range; x 60 px inside the edges.
- E_SCHEMA_PATTERN: an id or color in the wrong form → Ids lowercase_with_underscores; colors #rrggbb.
- E_SCHEMA_FORM: an "at" or "to" in the wrong form → Use one of the four at forms; to is {x}, {near} or {exit}.
- E_SCHEMA_SIZE: too many items or the script is too big → Use fewer items.
- E_TEXT_LENGTH: text too long → Shorten it (say 40, text_pop 16, caption 80).
- E_CAST_UNKNOWN: an id that is not in cast → Add it to cast or fix the id.
- E_CAST_ABSENT: a character used in a scene it is not placed in → Place it in the scene cast (hidden if it arrives later).
- E_BODY_UNKNOWN: unknown body plan → Use a body from 02_characters.md.
- E_APPEARANCE: unknown appearance option, or two things in the same place → Catalog options only; colors need their hair/outfit.
- E_FACE_UNKNOWN: unknown face → Use a face from 02_characters.md.
- E_LOCATION_UNKNOWN: a scene location that is neither a location id nor a theme → Use a location id or a theme.
- E_THEME_UNKNOWN: unknown theme → Use a theme from 05_places_and_objects.md.
- E_OBJECT_UNKNOWN: unknown object kind or object id → Use a catalog object, or an id placed in the scene.
- E_OBJECT_STATE: a state or change the object does not have → Use a state it has and a change that suits it.
- E_PROP_UNKNOWN: unknown prop → Use a prop from 05_places_and_objects.md.
- E_PARTNER_MISSING: a paired move without a partner in the scene → Add a partner who is in the scene.
- E_PARTNER_SELF: a character paired with itself → Pick someone else.
- E_MACRO_UNKNOWN: a macro this engine has no builder for → Use a macro from 06_story_tools.md.
- E_MACRO_PARAM: macro params missing or wrong (a winner who is not fighting, a finisher that is not an attack) → Required params, ids in the scene, a winner among the sides.
- E_ACTIVITY_OBJECT: an activity object that is not in the scene or that the activity cannot use → Place a set piece the activity can use.
- E_TRANSITION: a card without text or an iris without a target → Give the card text, the iris a target.
- E_SCENE_EMPTY: a scene with no beats and no duration → Add beats or a duration.
- E_DEFEAT_STYLE: a defeat style the audience does not allow (ghost is general only) → Kids: ko, faint, vanish, captured or flee.
- E_MOVE_RIG: a move the character's rig cannot play (a jab for a dog, a dog move for a stickman) → Use a move for that rig; generic walk, run, idle, sit and jump work for every rig.
- E_TARGET_RIG: an attack aimed at an animal (a quadruped) → Animals never take hits: target another character.
- E_MACRO_RIG: a fight macro names an animal (a quadruped) as a fighter → Leave the animal out of @fight, @gauntlet and @brawl; give it its own beats.
- E_REF_CHARACTER: no such character → Use an id from the cast, or world.
- E_REF_BEAT: no such beat (or one in another scene) → Point at a beat id in the same scene.
- E_REF_DUPLICATE: an id used twice (beat ids are unique across the whole story) → Make ids unique (prefix the scene id).
- E_REF_CYCLE: beats waiting for each other → Start one beat at a number instead.
- E_REF_ANCHOR: an anchor the beat or macro does not have → hit/windowOpen on attacks only; start/end always.
- E_MOVE_UNKNOWN: unknown move → Use a move from 03_moves.md.
- E_MOVE_TARGET: a character targeting itself → Target someone else.
- E_MOVE_OUTCOME: outcome on a non-attack → Remove outcome.
- E_MOVE_APPROACH: approach on a non-attack → Remove approach.
- E_MOVE_PARAM: a param the move does not take (or "to" on a move that does not walk) → Only the listed params, as numbers.
- E_MOVE_NEEDS_PROP: a move needing a prop the character does not hold → Give the character that prop.
- E_WORLD_UNKNOWN: unknown world command → Use a world command from the tables.
- E_WORLD_PARAM: a world command param missing or wrong → Add required params; stay in range.
- E_WORLD_FIELD: target/outcome/approach/say on a world beat → Remove those fields.
- E_FX_UNKNOWN: unknown fx → Use a beat fx from 04_effects_and_sound.md.
- E_CAMERA_START: the first camera key is not at 0 → Add a camera key at 0.
- E_CAMERA_FIELD: a camera mode missing its target(s), from or x → Add the target(s), from or x the mode needs.
- E_TEXT_GLYPH: characters the fonts cannot draw → Plain letters and punctuation; no emoji.
- E_TEXT_BLOCKED: a blocked word → Reword it.
- E_SIM_UNREACHABLE: an attack too far from its target (use approach run) → Add "approach": "run".
- E_SIM_APPROACH: an approach over 3 s (start closer) → Start them closer.
- E_SIM_DEAD_ACTOR: a knocked-out character acting → Add get_up or return first.
- E_SIM_UNRESOLVED: a beat whose anchor never happened → Anchor on .end of a beat that happens.
- E_SIM_DURATION: the video too short or too long → Make it 3-900 s.
- E_SIM_PARTNER_UNREACHABLE: a partner too far to walk to → Start them closer.
- E_SIM_OBJECT_OFFSTAGE: a ball or vehicle leaving the stage → Keep it on stage, or use exit.
- E_SIM_SCENE_LENGTH: a scene over 300 s → Split the scene.
- W_ATTACK_NO_TARGET: an attack without a target → Add a target.
- W_CONTRAST: a color hard to see on the background → Pick a color from the theme table.
- W_QUEUE_DRIFT: a beat started late because its character was busy → Chain it with after.
- W_PACING_GAP: over 2.5 s with nothing happening → Add a reaction, line or effect.
- W_NO_IMPACT: no hit lands → Land one hit.
- W_PACING_MONOTONE: more than 8 attacks in a row → Add a taunt, reaction or effect.
- W_NO_ENDING: no clear ending → End with a victory, KO, end card or fade.
- W_HEAVY_NO_EMPHASIS: a heavy hit without emphasis → Add slowmo or zoom_punch.
- W_REACH: sizes too different for the hit → Use a move that suits the sizes.
- W_NO_PROP: nothing to pick up or give → spawn_prop near them first.
- W_HIDDEN: a hidden character acting → Bring them in first (spawn, @enter).
- W_PARTICLE_BUDGET: too many effects at once → Fewer effects at once.
- W_DIALOGUE_FAST: a line too short to read, or talking over itself → Give the line more time.
- W_TEXT_SOFT: a strong word for the audience → Use the suggested word.
- W_KIDS_NO_HOPE: kids: vanished or petrified, never back → Bring them back with return.
- W_STORY_SHORT: a story under 300 s → Make it 300 s or more.
- W_FIGHT_SHORT: a fight video under 180 s → Make it 180 s or more.
- W_SCENE_STATIC: over 4 s of a scene where nothing moves → Add movement, a line or narration.
- W_CAST_UNUSED: a cast member no scene places → Place them in a scene or drop them.
- E_BUNDLE_AUDIENCE: a kids story declares a bundle that is not made for kids → Use a bundle that lists kids, or set meta.audience to general if that fits.
- E_BUNDLE_COMBO: two declared bundles do not work together: a move of one breaks on a body plan of the other → Use one of the two bundles.
- E_BUNDLE_DEPENDENCY: a declared bundle needs another bundle that the script does not declare → Declare the dependency too, with its hash.
- E_BUNDLE_HASH: a bundle with the declared id is loaded, but with another hash (different content) → Load the pinned bundle, or pin the loaded one if you mean it.
- E_BUNDLE_MISSING: a bundle the script declares in "bundles" is not loaded → Import the bundle (or pass --bundle to the tool), or remove it from "bundles".
- E_BUNDLE_UNDECLARED: a name with a colon (bundle:name) from a bundle the script does not declare → Add that bundle's {id, version, hash} line to "bundles".
- W_BUNDLE_UNUSED: a declared bundle that no name in the script uses → Remove it from "bundles", or use one of its entries.
- Version 3 scripts only: E_DEPTH_RANGE (a z (placement, set piece or to.z) is outside the scene's depth range); E_DEPTH_LAYER (a node gives both z and layer); E_LIGHT_UNKNOWN (an unknown light rig preset (scene or location light, set_light)); E_CAMERA_MOVE (an unknown named camera move (a v3 camera key move or set_camera)); E_LAYER_REF (a text, shape, mask or parent names a layer or shape that does not exist, or layer parents loop); E_REF_SCENE (a layer, text, shape or track names a scene that does not exist); E_TRACK_TARGET (a track target that is not keyable, or names a missing node); E_TRACK_KEYS (a key value of the wrong kind, two keys at one time, or a path or line missing its points); E_TRACK_EASE (an unknown easing on a key); E_TEXT_STYLE (an unknown text style); E_VIEW_BODY (a character is asked for a turnaround view its body plan does not have); E_AUDIO_TRACK (an audio track with an unknown mood, bed or SFX key, a missing field, or a duck rule under nothing); E_MARKER_UNKNOWN (a beat or sfx track starts at a marker that does not exist, or that is in another scene); E_TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN (a scene uses a template that is not in the catalog); E_TEMPLATE_PARAM (a template param is missing, unknown or of the wrong type).
